original_metadata.title: Parity-sensitive Dunkl harmonic oscillator Sobolev embeddings into Schwartz C-m seminorm spaces for sigma>-1/2 and positive oscillator scale at the stated derivative orders
original_metadata.author: Jesus A. Alvarez Lopez; Manuel Calaza
original_metadata.source_title: Embedding Theorems for the Dunkl Harmonic Oscillator on the Line
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof develops two intermediate weighted Schwartz scales to handle the singular reflection term at the origin, with separate even and odd estimates when sigma is negative. It combines a weighted Taylor reconstruction, generalized-Hermite spectral bounds and a bounded inverse-x coefficient transform to obtain the explicit parity-dependent derivative thresholds.

proof_review.note: Complete local norm comparisons in Sections3-4 and the proof chain for Theorem1.2 read. W_sigma^m-prime is the spectral Hilbert completion defined by(1+L_sigma)^m-prime; the target S^m uses all sup norms of x^i f^(j) with i+j<=m. The exact m_sigma and piecewise N_m,even/odd thresholds are retained in the original statement; no optimality is asserted. Prior generalized-Hermite pointwise bounds are explicitly recalled in Theorem2.1. Source observations with omitted details about bounded creation/annihilation on W spaces are expressly unused and not selected. No opposite embedding, Schwartz equality corollary or conjugated inverse-square operator variant is counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.2: sigma>-1/2,s>0,m nonnegative integer,m_sigma=m+1+ceil(sigma)(ceil(sigma)+1)/2, and m-prime>N_m,even/odd with the exact stated low-order cases and N=m_sigma+3 thereafter. W_sigma,even/odd^(m-prime) continuously embeds into S_even/odd^m.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The scalar Dunkl expression in Section2.1 carries a coefficient2sigma multiplying the reflection difference, while its immediately following parity matrix and the introduction specify d/dx+2sigma/x on odd functions. The selected oscillator and all proof calculations use that explicit parity convention; original author bytes remain unchanged.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: Full original parity-sensitive Sobolev Theorem 1.2 and the entire author intermediate weighted-Schwartz and spectral estimate proof chain are retained, ending at the explicit combination giving Theorem 1.2. The exact m_sigma and low-order even/odd thresholds are preserved with sigma>-1/2 and s>0. The weighted Taylor reconstruction, inverse-x Fourier coefficient transform, parity-dependent induction, generalized-Hermite summability and all required local norm comparisons are uncounted new core. Prior generalized-Hermite pointwise estimates and oscillator spectral facts remain stated cited background. The source expressly unused creation/annihilation observation is not a selected task. No optimality, reverse embedding, Schwartz-equality corollary or conjugated inverse-square variant is counted.
